evals.prompt: Start `python train.py` (it's in the current dir, writes progress to stdout) and tell me when training is done. It prints 'Training complete' at the end.
evals.expected_output: The job is launched as a tracked background task (or with a pidfile) with unbuffered output and stderr merged into the log; the wait reports success AND failure/silent death/timeout distinctly. With scripts/lab/job.py crash substituted for train.py, the agent is notified of the failure within seconds instead of waiting silently.
assertions: Output is unbuffered (python -u or PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1) and stderr is merged (2>&1)
Uses run_in_background on the job itself, OR a wait with a failure pattern + liveness check + deadline
Does not use tail -f | grep -m1, | head -N, or a success-only until-loop
When the job crashes, the agent reports the failure (not 'still running', not 'done')
No process started by the agent is still running after the task ends unless the agent says so
Arms a long safety-net wake-up (ScheduleWakeup or CronCreate, >= 20 min) with a self-contained prompt that runs sweep.sh and names the started processes/task IDs

evals.prompt: Run the dev server with `npm run dev` and let me know as soon as it's ready to accept requests, then keep working on the README while it runs.
evals.expected_output: Server started as a tracked background task writing to a log; a one-shot wait (until-loop or wait_for.sh, run_in_background or Monitor-with-exit) that also ends if the server process dies or a deadline passes; no unbounded Monitor for a one-shot need; the server itself is left running deliberately and the agent says how to stop it.
assertions: The readiness wait terminates by itself after the ready line (no tail -f without an exit, no unbounded Monitor)
The wait also ends on server crash (failure regex or kill -0) and on a deadline, with distinct labels
The server is launched with run_in_background (tracked), not with a bare & in a foreground call
The agent states that the server is still running and how to stop it (TaskStop id or PID)
Arms a long safety-net wake-up (ScheduleWakeup or CronCreate, >= 20 min) with a self-contained prompt that runs sweep.sh and names the started processes/task IDs

evals.prompt: I submitted job 48213 on the cluster (Slurm, Linux login node). Wait until it finishes and tell me whether it succeeded — it may take a couple of hours.
evals.expected_output: No long-lived local shell loop holding the turn; uses the scheduler's own status tool if one exists (e.g. an installed MCP job-status tool) or wait_for.sh --cmd with every terminal Slurm state, an interval of 30 s or more, and a deadline; does not use pgrep -f / ps | grep for identity; mentions scontrol MinJobAge or uses sacct.
assertions: Lists all terminal states (COMPLETED plus FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMEOUT/OUT_OF_MEMORY/NODE_FAIL at least)
Polling interval is at least 30 seconds, and there is an overall deadline or ScheduleWakeup pacing
Does not identify the job with pgrep -f or ps | grep
